title: SharePoint: create, upload and publish HTML pages, with Copilot drafting
summary: The briefing is supported by Microsoft's notice, the roadmap record and the cited Learn documentation. The licence assignment and site restriction controls are documented, and the briefing clearly distinguishes confirmed behaviour from unresolved HTML upload and billing details.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page.
2. Select a product.
3. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the selected licence.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: The minimum licence assignment role is License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites.
2. Select the site you want to configure.
3. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery on the site.
claims.quote:
Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
You can enable Restricted Content Discovery from the SharePoint admin center or by using PowerShell.
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance controls; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery removes the Copilot button, AI actions menus and Create pages with AI entry points on a site.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery also removes AI-powered entry points from these SharePoint sites. Users don't see entry points such as the Copilot button, AI actions menus (including creating agents), or Create pages with AI.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery restricts organisation-wide search and Copilot content discovery.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires Copilot licensing and SharePoint Advanced Management availability.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Restricted Content Discovery as a temporary governance control.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is designed as a temporary governance control that gives organizations time to review and right-size access while continuing their Copilot deployment.

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly say whether Restricted Content Discovery removes + New > HTML page or HTML upload.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint HTML page disable admin control Restricted Content Discovery Site AI upload. Read restricted-content-discovery and Copilot getting-started; neither names the HTML page menu or upload route among removed entry points.

claims.claim: Microsoft's readiness guidance alternatively labels the site setting Restrict content discovery > On.
claims.quote: Under Restrict content discovery, select On. Then select Save.

claims.claim: The Site AI settings panel opens through Settings > Site AI.
claims.quote: To open the panel, go to Settings > Site AI.

claims.claim: Site AI settings can hide the Copilot button on site pages for site visitors only.
claims.quote: Hide the Copilot button on site pages for site visitors only.

claims.claim: The preview KnowledgeAgent PowerShell availability controls are retiring.
claims.quote: Copilot in SharePoint is retiring the PowerShell commands used to opt tenants and sites in or out during preview—KnowledgeAgentScope, KnowledgeAgentSelectedSitesList, and KnowledgeAgentSelectedSitesListOperation.

claims.claim: After 1 November 2026, Learn directs administrators to use Site AI settings and Restricted Content Discovery to manage availability.
claims.quote:
Existing PowerShell settings remain in effect until November 1, 2026.
After November 1, 2026, manage availability by using Site AI settings and Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: The Copilot getting-started page and MC1479517 describe no setting specific to HTML pages.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint HTML page disable admin control Restricted Content Discovery Site AI upload. Read Copilot getting-started and MC1479517 in full; they describe general Copilot controls, not an HTML-pages-specific switch.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.

claims.claim: The Site AI settings panel lets site owners manage AI interaction on their site.
claims.quote: The Site AI settings panel lets site owners manage how users interact with AI on their site, including Copilot in SharePoint.
